newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks start new financial year softer.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks start new financial year softer.

text.p: The Australian share market slipped from its recent heady levels at the start on Tuesday amid early profit-taking as Monday's end of financial year window-dressing started to unravel.
A firmly underpinned market quickly steadied, however, with the benchmark All Ordinaries index bouncing off an early low of 2,701.1 to lose just 3.6 points to 2,722.3.

"We were up 24 points yesterday which was probably a bit much and I think you have seen some profit-taking on that, but as well, it's the first day of the new (financial) year," said Morgan Stockbroking dealer, John O'Neill.
"Obviously, the window-dressing yesterday may be being unwound today."

Brokers said the handover proceedings in Hong Kong had not impacted the local market, with any effect likely to be confined to other markets in the region that were more directly connected to the issue.
"I would be doubtful it's had any effect here," said a Sydney-based dealer of a European investment house.
"It's more of an issue for the Asian markets further down the track."

Most of the leading stocks showed modest losses as profit takers cashed in, although media giant News Corp was slightly firmer, up five cents at A$6.40 (A$4.80), after its ADRs strengthened in New York trading.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about five to four, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
